Kishor Kant And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 5

Author: Krishan Pahal

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:101718
Court No. - 75

Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 5428 of 2024
Applicant :- Kishor Kant And Another

Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Rajesh K.S. Chaudhary
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Gaurav Srivastav
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Rajesh K.S. Chaudhary, learned counsel for the applicants and Sri Gaurav Srivastav,
learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri Amit Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State and also perused the material available on record.
3.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicants in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 106 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 308, 323, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Delhi Gate, District Aligarh, with a prayer to enlarge them on anticipatory bail.

Kishor Kant And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 5 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163176467/
1 4.

entities.text: Kishor Kant And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, the husband of the informant is stated to have subjected her to cruelty by demanding Rs. 40 thousand per month from her parents and which were transferred to him through G PAY and later on, was being given in cash.
In the night of 30.3.2024, the applicant and all the family members are stated to have assaulted her at about 1.30 am, thereby causing injuries to her.
5. Learned counsel for the applicants has stated that the applicants are maliciously being prosecuted in the present case due to ulterior motive and have the apprehension of their arrest.
The applicants have nothing to do with the said offence as alleged by the prosecution.
It is next stated that the FIR is delayed by more than one day and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
Learned counsel has also stated that even the medical examination of the injured person has been conducted at 11.20 am on 31.3.2024.

It is stated that the applicants are married brother-in-law (Nandoi) and sister-in-law (Nand) of the injured person and have nothing to do with the said offence, as they live separately to the husband of the informant and other family members.
Learned counsel has further stated that the case of the applicants is at a different footing to the other named co-accused persons.

Learned counsel has stated that even the FIR does not indicate the demand of any dowry, rather it is a case of transfer of certain money to the husband of the victim.
6.

Learned counsel has placed much reliance upon the judgement of Supreme Court passed in Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam vs The State of Bihar, reported in 2022 (6) SCC 599, whereby it has been categorically stated that the Courts should be careful in proceeding against the distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam vs The State of Bihar, reported in 2022 (6) SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out.
7. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicants to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against them.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicants have also been touched upon at length.
It is further submitted that the applicants have no criminal antecedents.
In case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicants is allowed, they will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.

8. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail on the ground that the injuries are grievous in nature and the injured person has sustained 14 stitches to her skull, which is a vital part of the body.

9. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, the fact that the applicants are the married relatives of the victim, who lives separately to the husband of the informant and in view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98", the applicants are entitled to be granted anticipatory bail in this case.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. Without expressing any opinion upon ultimate merits of the case either ways which may adversely affect the trial of the case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicants is allowed.

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court below shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicants.

13. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicants shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
